"**Call Out My Name**" is a song by the Canadian singer-songwriter [The Weeknd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Weeknd "The Weeknd") from his debut extended play, _[My Dear Melancholy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/My\_Dear\_Melancholy "My Dear Melancholy")_ (2018). The song was co-written by The Weeknd and producer [Frank Dukes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frank_Dukes "Frank Dukes"), with musician [Nicolas Jaar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicolas_Jaar "Nicolas Jaar") receiving writing credits for the sampling of his 2016 song "[Killing Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sirens_(Nicolas_Jaar_album) "Sirens (Nicolas Jaar album)")". The song was sent to [rhythmic contemporary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhythmic_contemporary "Rhythmic contemporary") radio on April 10, 2018, as the EP's only single.

## Composition

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Call_Out_My_Name&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Composition")]

According to musicnotes.com, the song is performed in the key of [E♭ minor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E-flat_minor "E-flat minor") with a [tempo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tempo "Tempo") of 45 beats per minute[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Call_Out_My_Name#cite_note-2) in [compound duple (**6** **8**) time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duple_and_quadruple_metre "Duple and quadruple metre"). The chords alternate between G♯m and D♯m. The Weeknd's vocals span two octaves, from D♯3 to D♯5.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Call_Out_My_Name#cite_note-3)

## Critical reception

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Call_Out_My_Name&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Critical reception")]

[Alexis Petridis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexis_Petridis "Alexis Petridis") of _[The Guardian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Guardian "The Guardian")_ called it the least interesting track on _My Dear Melancholy_: "it offers up the kind of beige boo-hoo balladry that [Sam Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Smith "Sam Smith") specialises in, albeit tricked out with more interesting sonic touches: the piano sounding like it was recorded underwater, the rest of the track echoing and ghostly."[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Call_Out_My_Name#cite_note-4)

In 2022, _[Seventeen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seventeen\_(American\_magazine) "Seventeen (American magazine)")_ placed the song on its "46 Songs About Cheating If You Need To Cry Your Eyes Out" list.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Call_Out_My_Name#cite_note-5)

## Commercial performance

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Call_Out_My_Name&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Commercial performance")]

"Call Out My Name" earned the largest first-day [Spotify](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spotify "Spotify") stream count of any song released in 2018.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Call_Out_My_Name#cite_note-6) The song was also streamed 6 million times on its first day on [Apple Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apple_Music "Apple Music").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Call_Out_My_Name#cite_note-7) The song debuted at number one in his native Canada, Malaysia, Greece, and Slovakia, his first number one debut in the former two; as well as at number four on the US [_Billboard_ Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100") on the issue dated April 14, 2018, becoming his eighth top ten entry.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Call_Out_My_Name#cite_note-8) As of March 2020, the song has been certified 3× platinum in the United States.

Additionally, it also reached the top ten in Australia, Czech Republic, Denmark, Germany, Ireland, Lebanon, New Zealand, Norway, Portugal, United Kingdom and Sweden, top twenty, Austria, Finland, Hungary and The Netherlands, top thirty in Belgium (Wallonia), Mexico and Scotland and top forty in the [Flemish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flemish_region "Flemish region") region of Belgium, France and Italy. The song was certified diamond in Brazil, France[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Call_Out_My_Name#cite_note-9) and Greece, and multi-platinum in Australia, Canada, New Zealand, Poland and Portugal.
